fact: Colorado 811 says every Colorado property owner must contact it at least 48 hours ahead, not counting weekends, the day of notice or legal holidays, before any excavation, and lists landscaping and driving landscaping stakes into the ground among the examples, telling homeowners not to rely on a landscaper alone.
quote: All Colorado property owners must contact Colorado 811 at least 48 hours (excluding weekends, the day of the notification, and legal holidays) before beginning any excavation project – as required by Colorado law. Examples of work are: Landscaping (Don’t just rely on your landscaper to do it, if in doubt, contact 811 yourself). … Driving landscaping stakes into the ground
source_label: Colorado 811, Residential Property: Planning to Dig on Your Property?
notes: Read with a browser user agent on 2026-09-25. The same page also says state law requires contact at least two full business days before digging, not counting the day of notification. Turf is fastened with 6-inch spikes driven into the base, which is why the stakes line matters on a DIY job.

fact: Colorado 811 says whoever performs the excavation, a homeowner included, must submit the locate request in their own name, that 811 does not mark private lines on the property, and that having private lines located separately is the excavator's responsibility.
quote: The party performing the actual excavation (home/property owner, contractor, landscaper, etc.) must submit the locate request in their own/company name as an authorized user of the account. … Private underground lines are owned by the owner of the property and will not be located or marked by 811 as part of this request. It is the responsibility of the excavator to have private utility lines located separately from the Colorado 811 locate request service.
notes: On a DIY job the homeowner is the excavator, so the ticket and the private locate are the homeowner's to arrange.

fact: SYNLawn's DIY installation guidelines highly recommend a sod cutter on projects over 150 square feet, a rented vibratory plate compactor on projects larger than 150 square feet and a drop seed spreader for sand infill above 150 square feet, have each layer of sand brushed in with a power broom or stiff broom, and recommend help carrying cut turf rolls because of their weight.
quote: Note: It is highly recommended for any projects over 150 sq. ft. to use a sod cutter to remove existing sod. … Note: It is highly recommended to rent a vibratory plate compactor for any projects larger than 150 sq. ft. … Also note that it is highly recommended to have help carrying and moving custom cut turf rolls due to the weight of the product. … Note: For projects larger than 150 sq. ft. it is highly recommended to use a drop seed spreader to add your sand. … With each layer of sand, the turf needs to be vigorously brushed using a power broom, Grandi Groomer or coarse bristle nylon broom.
source_label: SYNLawn, DIY Installation Guidelines for SYNLawn Artificial Grass (Lowe's product document)

fact: SYNLawn's DIY guidelines have the base rock ordered from a local rock yard and dumped in the street or driveway, then moved in by wheelbarrow at about 13 to 16 loads per ton, so the roughly 6 tons its rule gives for 600 square feet at 3 inches deep works out to about 78 to 96 wheelbarrow loads.
quote: This material will need to be ordered through a local rock yard and will be dumped in the street or driveway as directed by you. … For each ton of aggregate, you are looking at approximately 13-16 wheelbarrows full that will need to be hauled to the project area from the staged dumping area. … Haul base material from street using wheelbarrows and dump in desired area until you create a 3”- 4” base.
source_label: SYNLawn, DIY Installation Guidelines for SYNLawn Artificial Grass (Lowe's product document)
notes: 78 to 96 is arithmetic, not SYNLawn's figure: 6 tons × 13 and × 16 loads. The 6 tons for 600 sq ft at 3 in comes from SYNLawn's 1 ton per 100 sq ft rule (what-base-goes-under-artificial-turf.synlawn-diy-tonnage).

fact: SYNLawn's DIY guidelines warn that measuring mistakes cost money, suggest ordering 10 to 20 percent more turf than the area's square footage where there are curves and irregular shapes, say to over-measure slightly so the job isn't left short, and say each seam needs the adhesive maker's curing time.
quote: Mistakes can cost money. Measure your job carefully. If you have many curves and irregular shapes, we recommend adding 10- 20% more turf than your area’s actual square footage. … Slightly over- measure being cautious so you are not left short on the job. … The seam will need time to dry or cure based on recommended curing times by adhesive manufacturer. … Take your time on the seams.
source_label: SYNLawn, DIY Installation Guidelines for SYNLawn Artificial Grass (Lowe's product document)
notes: The line breaks in the PDF put a space after the hyphens in "10- 20%" and "over- measure"; the quote keeps them as extracted.

fact: ForeverLawn's general landscape installation guidelines say its turf is best installed by authorized ForeverLawn dealers and installers, list a vibratory plate tamper and a hand tamper for the base and a loop-pile carpet cutter for trimming seam edges, list crumb rubber infill among the supplies, and suggest renting a motorized power broom.
quote: The product is best installed by authorized ForeverLawn dealers and installers. … Vibratory plate tamper for compacting the stone. … Hand tamper (10”x10” or larger) for compacting edges and hard to reach places. … Crumb rubber infill. … we recommend a carpet tool called a Crain 303 Loop Pile Carpet Cutter (or similar) with the ForeverLawn bullnose attachment to remove the factory edges. … If available, you may want to rent a motorized power broom from an equipment rental store.
source_label: ForeverLawn General Landscape Installation Guidelines (M1374 Rev. 05/19)
notes: The crumb rubber line matters locally: Firestone's code bans crumb rubber infill (firestone-fdc-16.6.4-turf-specs). A maker's generic guide is not a town's spec.

fact: ForeverLawn says every ForeverLawn dealer provides at least two years of coverage on the installation, and ties its coverage to professional installations.
quote: That’s why every ForeverLawn dealer provides a minimum two-year installation warranty, supported by expert guidance and ongoing service. … By offering warranties with professional installations, ForeverLawn ensures accountability, transparency, and support you can rely on.

fact: SYNLawn's consumer coverage page says the coverage does not extend to damage caused by improper installation, misuse, abuse, neglect or acts of nature such as floods or fires.
quote: The warranty does not extend to damage caused by improper installation, misuse, abuse, neglect, or acts of nature like floods or fires.
